spoilers: none: general Barovian attitudes only; no module secrets, hidden identities or twists

faceless: our figures are faceless: no race is judged by its eyes or face, and every reaction is carried by the body

tiers.name: Outlander
tiers.reason: Barovians are human, and they still don't trust you. You came out of the mists, and in their experience nothing good comes out of the mists. They answer, but they keep a hand on the door.

tiers.name: Odd
tiers.reason: Short folk and fair folk out of grandmothers' tales. The valley knows the dusk elves, so elves are strange but real; dwarves, halflings and gnomes look like a story walking. People stare, whisper and charge a little more, but they deal with you.

tiers.name: Uncanny
tiers.reason: Too tall, too grey, too pale, the wrong colour altogether. Nothing in Barovia's stories explains them, and what the valley can't explain it keeps at arm's length: served at the end of the counter, talked about, never asked in.

tiers.name: Feared
tiers.reason: Horns and tails, scales and snouts, tusks, a witch's crown, a dead man's stitches: the shapes the priests' sermons and the old stories give to devils, dragons, witches and the walking dead. People make the sign against evil, bar their doors and send for the watch.

tiers.name: Monstrous
tiers.reason: Goblin faces, fur, fangs, beaks, beasts that walk like men: the things mothers warn their children about, and in Barovia every child knows the wolves are real. People scream, run, pray or pick up a pitchfork. Nobody sells to it and nobody opens a door.

hood.what: a hood, a wide hat, a headscarf or a cap pulled low
hides: a crown or mark on the head
hood.effect: race tier minus the race's hood_steps
hood.cost: none: Barovians wear hoods and headscarves in this weather, so a hood draws no looks
hood.library_note: the library's hoods, headscarf and wide hats (review 8) are NPC variants; players get their own look-alike hood, since NPC gear stays unique

muffled.what: hood plus a face scarf or veil, gloves, and a long cloak or coat
muffled.effect: race tier minus the race's muffle_steps, but never below T2
muffled.why_floor: a stranger who hides every inch of skin is suspicious in himself

disguise.what: a disguise kit, Disguise Self, Alter Self, a Hat of Disguise, or a race's own disguise magic or shapechanging

size_floor.why: nobody passes as a grown human at a halfling's or a giant's height

disguise.no_disguise_why: a human disguise can't change the body's shape
disguise.unmask_check: on close contact (talking, trading, a guard's inspection, a search), once per NPC per day: the NPC's Wisdom (Insight) against the disguise DC: 10 + the wearer's Deception bonus with a kit, or the spell save DC for magic

unmasked.tier: race tier + 1 (max T4) in that settlement for the rest of the visit

formula: 1. Race tier: from the race table. An alias uses its parent's tier.
2. Cover: hooded = race tier - hood_steps; muffled = max(2, race tier - muffle_steps); disguised = 0 (1 if shorter than 1.4 m or 2.1 m and taller) until unmasked.
3. Events: unmasked in this settlement = race tier + 1 (max 4) for the visit; seen changing shape here = 4 for the visit.
4. Party tier: the highest seen tier among the members this NPC can see (the worst visible member counts).
5. Viewer: Vistani and dusk elves halve it, rounding down.
6. Relief: a vouch (-1, or -2 from a local), a passed test (-1), standing (Tolerated -1, Trusted -2). Together at most 2 steps, and never below T1 while a non-human is visible.
7. Penalties: standing Distrusted +1, Hated +2. For guards and crowds only: a drawn weapon or open magic +1. At night, for doors, gates and crowds: +1.
8. Clamp to 0..4. The effect tables use this effective tier.

combine.present: a member counts if the NPC can see them: within 12 m and in line of sight, or in the same room
combine.group_actions: shops, inns, door knocks and gates use the party tier: the highest seen tier among members present
combine.street: each villager reacts to the highest-tier member inside their notice radius
combine.dialogue: the highest seen tier among the speaker and members within 6 m
combine.many_strangers: two or more members at the party tier: rumours about the party count x1.5
combine.familiar_sight: from the second day in a settlement, crowds react one tier lower to members they have already seen (never below T1 for a non-human); shops, doors and guards don't soften
combine.proxy: a member who is served can shop for the party; if the shopkeeper saw the whole party together that day, the proxy pays at the party tier - 1
combine.companions: animal companions, mounts, familiars and summons count at the tier of what they look like: a horse, dog, cat or bird T0, a wolf T4

alternatives.average_up: the party's average seen tier, rounded up
alternatives.worst_softened: the worst member's tier, minus 1 if at least half of those present read T0

vouch.who: a party member who reads T0, present in the conversation
vouch.check: Persuasion, DC 10 + 2 x the tier being vouched for
vouch.success: -1 step with that NPC, for good
vouch.fail: no change; that NPC won't hear another vouch that day
vouch.local: a Barovian travelling with the party vouches automatically for -1, or -2 on a passed check at the same DC
vouch.risk: if a vouched member causes trouble in that settlement, every vouch there lapses

test.what: a wary NPC's superstitious test: touch the holy symbol, hold the garlic, take a splash of holy water, step over the salted threshold
test.pass: every playable race passes; -1 step with that NPC for good, and +3 standing
test.why: the test is theatre: what the villager needs is to see you submit

hood_down.what: show your face before you're asked
hood_down.effect: that NPC can't unmask you, and +2 standing (once per member per settlement)

standing.hated_extra: guards refuse the party at the gate

relief.how: relief lowers the effective tier, and every table then applies at the new tier: a vouch at a T3 shop means T2 service
relief.why_floor: they will accept you; they won't forget what you are

weapon_drawn.when: any member has a weapon out inside a settlement

open_magic.when: a visible spell cast in sight of locals (healing excepted), for 1 in-game hour

shapechange_seen.when: a member changes shape in sight of locals: wild shape, polymorph, a changeling's change, a shifter's shift

viewers.why: the Vistani have travelled beyond the valley and go by manners and trade, not looks; the dusk elves are outsiders to Barovians themselves (draft value: see open question 7)

shops.on_top_of: each shop's own markup (dungine.v2's village shop charges 2.6x item value to everyone)
served: at the end of the counter; coin goes in a dish, never hand to hand
at the door or through a hatch, never inside
not served: the door is barred and the sign turned
inn: the worst room, paid in advance
no room in the house: the attic or the stable loft
tavern: served last, at the far table
served last, in a corner; half the room leaves
not let in; the keeper blocks the door

dialogue.addressee: from T2 the NPC answers the lowest-tier member present, talking past the speaker; if nobody lower is present, a generic NPC gives one line and ends
option_gates: personal options (family, gossip, favours, local history) hidden
business only: trade, directions, the task at hand
generic NPCs don't talk (a bark and a reaction); key NPCs keep only their story options

tokens.{human}: the lowest-tier member present (the one the NPC talks to)
tokens.{called}: what villagers call the judged member's kind

villager: *He looks at your boots, not your face.* Outlanders. Mind where you walk, and mind who you talk to.
*She looks down at you, then at your friends, as if one of them might explain you.* ...And what are you meant to be?
*He answers {human}, not you.* Your friend there. Does it understand us? Keep it away from the well.
*She makes the sign against evil and keeps her hand up between you.* I've nothing for you. Go back to whatever made you.
*He backs into a doorway with a spade up between you.* Stay back! Stay back, or I call the watch!
shopkeeper: Coin first. Outlander coin, I weigh twice.
Same prices for your kind. *He writes a new price over the old one.* Plus the trouble.
I'll sell. You stand there, at the end. Coin in the dish.
Not in here. If {human} wants something, {human} can come in alone.
*The bolt goes home. Through the door:* Closed. Closed to you.
guard: Name and business. Weapons stay sheathed in town.
Business? *He looks {name} up and down, slowly.* Your friend's a long way from home.
Halt. Hood down. *A long look.* What in the name of all that's holy are you?
*His hand is on his sword before you've stopped walking.* That one stays outside.
*He shouts over his shoulder:* To the gate! There's a monster on the road!
door: *The door opens a hand's width.* Who's asking?
*Through the door:* We've nothing. Try the tavern.
*A slot opens at head height and snaps shut.* Go away.
*The bar drops.* Go back to the dark you came from!
*The light behind the shutters goes out. Somebody inside is praying.*

lines.vouch: [VOUCH] They're with me. I'll answer for them.
lines.vouch_pass: *She looks from you to {name} and back. Her hand comes down, slowly.* ...On your head, then.
lines.vouch_fail: *She doesn't even look at you.* Then you're a fool, and I don't deal with fools either.
lines.test_offer: *He holds a braid of garlic out at arm's length.* Touch it. Go on.
lines.test_pass: *Nothing happens. He almost looks disappointed.* ...Fine. Fine.
lines.test_refuse: *He steps back.* That's what I thought.

crowds.alarm: at T4 at least one villager raises the alarm if guards are within earshot
stalls: stalls within 12 m close for 1 hour
stalls within 24 m close for the day

gate: asks your business and watches you in
halts you: questions, 'hood down', then lets you in
by day: in, weapons peace-bonded; at night: refused
in_town: heads follow the member within 10 m
one guard walks the party's route at about 10 m for 1 hour
one guard shadows the party at 6 to 8 m for the whole visit
challenged on sight: weapons out, ordered out of town, two warnings, then a fight only if the party pushes past or draws
guards.never: guards never attack on sight: they bar the way, warn twice, and fight only if the party forces past or draws on them

knock: opens a hand's width and talks through the gap; lets you in by day on Persuasion DC 12
talks through the closed door; doesn't open
talks through a slot or shutter, then shuts it
shutters_reopen: 1 hour after the party leaves the radius
the next morning, if nothing else happened
doors.shops: a T4 seen within 24 m: nearby shops turn the sign and bar the door for the day (hatch trade if Tolerated)
doors.holy_ground: T3 and up: the priest asks for the test at the door; refusing means staying outside

standing_events.event: weapon drawn on a local, or a brawl
gift to the church or the poor (10 gp or more, once a day)
helped a villager (a small task, healing)
cleared a threat to the settlement

spread.why: Barovians believe the worst: bad news travels twice as well as good

rumours.forewarned: once any rumour about a member reaches a settlement, that member's first sighting there doesn't set off a panic: people gather at a distance to stare, and guards meet the party at the gate
rumours.journal: What they say: every rumour the party overhears goes into the journal, with the place and the day

barks.seen_odd: Did you see the little one with the beard? Like somebody's grandfather, cut off at the knees.
barks.seen_uncanny: A giant stooped under the tavern door this morning. Had to.
barks.seen_feared: Horns. I saw horns on it, under the hood.
barks.seen_feared_2: They say it's one of his. Sent down to count us.
barks.seen_monstrous: A goblin-thing, walking the road like a man, and the outlanders let it.
barks.unmasked: It wore a man's face. Wore it like a coat.
barks.shapechange: It went down on all fours in the square. I saw it change.
barks.deed_small: The horned one carried the widow's firewood. I saw it myself. It didn't burn her.
barks.deed_big: They cleared the wolves off the north road. Whatever they are, they did that.
barks.forewarned: It's them. The ones from the village. The one with the tail.

ui.portrait_icon: a small icon on each portrait: how Barovia sees this member right now (open shutter at T0 to barred door at T4); it changes when the hood goes up or down
ui.journal: the What they say page, and each settlement's standing band

safety: Quest-safe: key NPCs always talk (a colder opener, fewer extras), story doors always open, and anything the story needs can always be bought or found. Suspicion changes the price and the mood, never whether the campaign can be finished.
No ambushes: guards bar the way, warn twice, and fight only if the party forces the issue.
Players can always see why: the portrait icon, the journal and the barks explain a closed door.

knobs.what: the whole system on or off
scales price, sell and DC changes and notice radii: value = neutral + (default - neutral) x intensity
every race one tier milder or harsher
move any race to another tier, by profile id
what shops pay you, per tier

knobs.default: -1 (-2 from a local), DC 10 + 2 x tier

knobs.what: how far vouches, tests and standing can bring a tier down
0 lets trusted non-humans read as Outlanders
per-settlement wariness; equal everywhere in this draft, so nothing hints at what each town is like

villagers.does: the head turns to the stranger for a beat, then back to work
stops work; head and shoulders turn and follow the stranger; hands go still
villagers.procedural: partly: look-at on a still pose

villagers.does: two villagers lean their heads together, one hand raised beside the head; both glance at the party
villagers.when: T1+, and while a rumour is fresh

villagers.does: an elbow to a neighbour, then a low point at hip height
a slow shake with the chin down
one step back, weight on the back foot, hands drawn up to the chest
folds the arms high, squares the shoulders, lifts the chin: a closed stance
turns a shoulder, then the back, head down
a walk with hunched shoulders and the head turned toward the stranger, drifting to the far side of the street
one hand closes on a pendant or holy symbol at the chest; the other covers it
steps between a child and the stranger and sweeps the child behind the coat or skirts
the child ducks behind the adult and peeks round
the child edges toward the stranger, head tilted, one hand out, until pulled away
the valley's sign against evil: fingertips to the brow, then to the heart, then the hand thrust out flat toward the stranger and held
a sharp turn of the head and a spit to the side
startles; what they carry falls; the hands fly up
backs away facing the stranger, palms out, small steps
a fast hunched walk, arms tight, head low, one glance back
pulls the door shut from inside and drops the bar
leans out of a window, pulls both shutters in and latches them
villagers.kind: one-shot, upper body in the window

villagers.does: cups the lamp and blows it out; the window goes dark
a hunched run, arms pulled in, a look back every few strides
drops to a crouch with the arms over the head, trembling
drops to the knees, hands clasped at the chest, rocking
the head thrown back and both hands raised beside it, then an arm pointing at the stranger
snatches up a pitchfork, spade, cudgel or torch and brings it across the body in both hands (the across-the-chest grip)
holds the tool out with short jabs, feet planted, giving half a step between jabs
palm out and a firm head shake; the other hand flat on the counter or ledger
slides a dish across for the coin, never hand to hand, then tips the coin out
pushes the goods across at arm's length, leaning back
turns the sign and pulls the hatch or counter flap shut
steps into the path, one hand raised flat, the other on the hilt
a resting hand on the hilt while the head tracks the stranger
plants the feet and holds the spear or halberd across the chest to block the way (the across-the-chest grip)
draws and holds the weapon low and ready
villagers.when: T3-T4, or when a party weapon is drawn

villagers.does: a sweeping wave of the hand: move along
fingers to the front of the head for a whistle, or an arm raised, calling another guard
walks alongside at a set distance, head locked on the stranger
opens the door a hand's width and talks through the gap, one hand on the door edge
a slot in the door or shutter opens; a hand and the shadow of a head show; it snaps shut
a small nod of recognition
a hand on the heart and a short bow
villagers.when: Tolerated or better, after a deed

villagers.does: holds out a small gift in both hands: bread, a garlic braid, a candle
the shoulders drop and the hands open: the way back from any wary pose
villagers.when: after a vouch or a passed test

villagers.does: holds a holy symbol or a garlic braid out at arm's length, leaning back, waiting
flicks a few drops of holy water at the stranger, then peers

party.does: both hands lift the hood over the head
both hands push the hood back
hands open and out, palms up: I mean no harm
the voucher sets a hand on the companion's shoulder
stands still, chin up, arms a little out, while the test is done

props.does: opens a hand's width and holds
the bar drops into its brackets
both shutters swing in and latch
a shop sign turns to its closed side
a door slot slides open and shut

animations.note: faceless: head, shoulders, hands, feet and props carry every reaction; the kit's head turn, bow, stoop and lean do much of it

open_questions.question: How harsh should it be by default?

options.text: Mild: intensity 0.5, and every race one tier milder.
Book: the values in this draft.
Harsh: intensity 1.5, and shops also refuse Feared members.

open_questions.question: Does the worst member count most?

options.text: Yes: the worst visible member sets the tier for everything the party does together.
No: use the party's average, rounded up.
Mostly: the worst member, minus one step if at least half of those present read as human.

open_questions.question: How far can good deeds take a non-human?

options.text: Down to Odd at best: accepted, never forgotten.
All the way: at Trusted they read as Outlanders.
One step at most, ever.
Risky: unmasked is worse than honest (one tier worse for the visit, standing -15).
Safe: unmasked just means back to the normal tier.
None: players can't disguise their race.

open_questions.question: The borderline races: orc (Feared), drow and the grey-skinned half-elves (Uncanny), dhampir (Uncanny), goliath and firbolg (Uncanny), dragonborn (Feared). Move any?

options.text: Keep them as drafted.
Move some (say which, and where).

open_questions.question: Magic in a character's look, like Chai'rn's glowing tendrils: does it count?

options.text: Race only; casting a spell in public counts +1 for an hour.
A permanent glow counts +1 while it shows (a hood covers Chai'rn's).
Magic never counts.

open_questions.question: The Vistani and the dusk elves as onlookers:

options.text: Half as wary as Barovians.
As wary as Barovians.
Not wary at all.
Mild in-world names (horned one, devil's get, tusker, bogey), never about skin colour.
None: they only describe (the tall one, the one with the tail).
Yes: an icon on each portrait for how Barovia sees that member right now, and a What they say journal page.
No: players learn it by playing.

open_questions.question: Party members' own reactions (a short bark when a door slams on them)?

options.text: Yes, short and occasional.
No.
Curious, not afraid, until a parent pulls them away.
Afraid, like the adults.
